**Likely root cause:** The DaemonSet nvidia-operator-validator in the gpu-operator namespace has not completed its rollout for at least 15 minutes, likely due to unschedulable pods or failing readiness checks on nodes.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check the status of the DaemonSet and its pods: `kubectl -n gpu-operator get daemonset nvidia-operator-validator -o yaml` and `kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods -l app=nvidia-operator-validator`
- Inspect pod events and logs for errors: `kubectl -n gpu-operator describe pods <pod-name>` and `kubectl -n gpu-operator logs <pod-name>`
- Verify node conditions and taints: `kubectl get nodes` and `kubectl describe nodes | grep -i taint`
- If pods are unschedulable, check resource requests/limits or node selectors in the DaemonSet spec.
- If a rollout is stuck due to a known issue, consider deleting the stuck pod to force recreation, or update the DaemonSet to a known-good version.

title: KubePodNotReady
body:
**Likely root cause:** The nvidia-operator-validator pod in the gpu-operator namespace is not ready, likely due to a failed validation or missing GPU resources.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check pod events and logs: `kubectl describe pod nvidia-operator-validator-q7pfp -n gpu-operator` and `kubectl logs nvidia-operator-validator-q7pfp -n gpu-operator`.
- Verify GPU nodes are available and have allocatable GPUs: `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPUs:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu`.
- Restart the validator pod: `kubectl delete pod nvidia-operator-validator-q7pfp -n gpu-operator` (it will be recreated by the DaemonSet).
- Check if the GPU operator is fully deployed and its daemonsets are ready: `kubectl get ds -n gpu-operator`.

title: KubeDaemonSetRolloutStuck
body:
**Likely root cause:** The DaemonSet nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset in namespace gpu-operator has not progressed for at least 15 minutes, likely due to unschedulable pods, image pull issues, or failing containers preventing the rollout from completing.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check DaemonSet rollout status: `kubectl rollout status daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n gpu-operator`
- Inspect pod status and events: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-operator -l daemonset=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` and `kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n gpu-operator`
- Look for common issues: insufficient node resources, taints/tolerations, image pull failures, or config errors in the DaemonSet spec.
- If a pod is stuck, delete it to force recreation: `kubectl delete pod <pod-name> -n gpu-operator`
- Apply fixes (e.g., update image tag, add resources, adjust tolerations) and monitor rollout progress for 15 minutes.

title: KubePodNotReady
body:
**Likely root cause:** The nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset pod in the gpu-operator namespace has been non-ready for over 15 minutes, likely due to a crash loop, image pull failure, or resource issue on the node.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check pod status and events: `kubectl describe pod -n gpu-operator nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-zxwdq` and `kubectl logs -n gpu-operator nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset-zxwdq`. 
- Verify the node is healthy and has GPU resources: `kubectl describe node <node-name> | grep -i gpu` (if applicable). 
- Check for resource limits/quotas or node pressure that may prevent the pod from starting. 
- If the container is in CrashLoopBackOff, consider restarting the daemonset: `kubectl rollout restart daemonset -n gpu-operator nvidia-device-plugin` (if a daemonset exists). 
- If the issue persists, escalate to the GPU operator team as it may affect GPU workloads on the node.

title: KubeDaemonSetRolloutStuck
body:
**Likely root cause:** DaemonSet nvidia-dcgm-exporter in namespace gpu-operator is stuck, likely due to pod scheduling issues or resource constraints on nodes.

**Suggested remediation:**
- Check DaemonSet status: `kubectl -n gpu-operator get daemonset nvidia-dcgm-exporter -o yaml` and `kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods -l app=nvidia-dcgm-exporter`
- Investigate pending pods: `kubectl -n gpu-operator describe pods <stuck-pod>` and look for events like insufficient resources, taints, or node selectors.
- Check node availability and resource pressure: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl top nodes`.
- If scheduling is blocked by taints, add tolerations to the DaemonSet spec or remove taints.
- If resource limits are too high, adjust requests/limits in the DaemonSet template and rollout restart: `kubectl -n gpu-operator rollout restart daemonset nvidia-dcgm-exporter`.
